hypothesis: A declared-tool-name final-token boundary is a sufficient runtime risk signal for the known confident wrong identifier, without a label-derived absolute position.

trigger.scope: Kimi K3 requests with one or more effective declared tools; research env gate only
trigger.definition: Tokenize every declared function name. For names containing at least two tokens, return a Budget96 floor for the next routed position iff committed generated IDs end with every name token except the final token.
trigger.reset: Return to the request/base policy on the following routed position unless another declared-name boundary matches.
explicit_non_goals: No entropy threshold, generic Fisher predictor, rollback, second pass, GSQ/Trellis decoder or request-wide Budget96.
One-token tool names are not rescued by this first discriminator.

validity: All three arms use one clean source commit and one executable hash.
The tool arm has no static position-budget environment value and no request-wide Budget96 marker.
The tool arm emits exactly one schema-rescue marker at base position 158 and returns one valid get_weather call for San Francisco.
The tool arm's generated IDs, logical traffic and final logits match the measured positional-singleton mechanism unless the difference is explicitly investigated before interpretation.

The non-tool on/off prompts have identical token hashes and their generated IDs, final logits, logical traffic and provider exact-fallback traffic are byte-identical; the on arm emits zero schema-rescue markers.

gate.go: All validity conditions pass. The trigger is then earned for a broader native-success tool suite plus false-positive tool-declared controls, still research-only.
gate.no_go: Any missed/extra marker, invalid get_weather result, or non-tool divergence rejects this trigger. Preserve the negative result and investigate a real framer-state signal instead of tuning token IDs on the fixture.
gate.production: No production transplant from this gate alone.
